sentences.text: Out in open water, you can pass another boat without asking her for anything.
In a narrow channel, sometimes you can’t get by unless she moves over.
When that’s the case, the overtaking vessel signals her intention with the whistle signals from Rule thirty-four.
We’ll learn those signals in lesson thirteen.
The vessel being overtaken, if she agrees, answers and takes steps to permit safe passing.
If she’s in doubt, she sounds the danger signal instead, and you stay behind her.
Even after she agrees, Rule thirteen still applies.
The overtaking vessel keeps clear until she’s past.
Agreement is permission to pass, not a transfer of responsibility.
When you’re nearing a bend, or any spot where something could hide another vessel, navigate with particular alertness and caution, and sound one prolonged blast.
Any vessel around the bend that hears you answers with one prolonged blast of her own.
Remember it this way: one long blast says, I’m coming around the corner.
